extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, program managers, legal/compliance staff responsible for implementing Section 504/Rehabilitation Act accessibility requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory obligations and procedural requirements for federal agencies to prevent discrimination on the basis of handicap and to make programs, activities, communications, facilities, procurement, and employment accessible and non‑discriminatory under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibition on discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not, on the basis of handicap, deny a qualified handicapped person the benefits of, be excluded from participation in, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity conducted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited actions enumerated include denying opportunity to participate in programs/activities; providing different or separate aid/benefits/services unless necessary to provide equally effective aid; denying opportunity to serve on planning or advisory boards; otherwise limiting enjoyment of rights/privileges/opportunities enjoyed by others. Also: the agency may not deny participation in nonseparate programs despite existence of separate programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using discriminatory criteria or administrative methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not, directly or through other arrangements, utilize criteria or methods of administration the purpose or effect of which would: (i) subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap; or (ii) defeat or substantially impair accomplishment of the objectives of a program or activity with respect to handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These limits apply to contracting, administration, and other methods used to run programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site and location selection constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the site or location of a facility, the agency may not make selections the purpose or effect of which would (i) exclude handicapped persons from, deny them the benefits of, or otherwise subject them to discrimination under any program or activity conducted by the agency; or (ii) defeat or substantially impair the accomplishment of the objectives of a program or activity with respect to handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site/location decisions must consider accessibility impacts and cannot be used to avoid serving handicapped persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement criteria restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency, in the selection of procurement contractors, may not use criteria that subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor selection processes must avoid criteria that would indirectly discriminate against qualified handicapped persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and certification non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not administer a licensing or certification program in a manner that subjects qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap, nor establish requirements for licensees/certified entities that subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: programs or activities of licensees/certified entities themselves are not covered by this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most integrated setting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall administer programs and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of qualified handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing among methods to achieve accessibility, give priority to those providing services in the most integrated setting appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility for existing facilities (viewed in its entirety)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall operate each program or activity so that the program or activity, when viewed in its entirety, is readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not necessarily require making each existing facility accessible. Exceptions include historic preservation considerations and where compliance would result in a fundamental alteration or undue financial/administrative burdens (agency bears burden to prove). If an alteration would cause such burdens, agency must take other actions that do not cause those burdens but ensure handicapped persons receive program benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to achieve program accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may comply through redesign of equipment, reassignment of services to accessible buildings, assignment of aides, home visits, delivery of services at alternate accessible sites, alteration of existing facilities, construction of new facilities, use of accessible rolling stock, or other methods that make programs readily accessible and usable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural changes are not required where other methods are effective. Agencies must prioritize methods offering the most integrated setting appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic preservation program accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: In historic preservation programs, agencies shall give priority to methods that provide physical access; if physical alteration is not required because of preservation or burden exceptions, alternative methods include using audio-visual materials to depict inaccessible portions, assigning guides to assist handicapped persons, or adopting other innovative methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When physical alteration would substantially impair historic features, agencies should use prioritized alternative methods to achieve accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall comply with obligations under § 500.150 by October 21, 1986; where structural changes are undertaken, such changes shall be made by August 22, 1989, and in any event as expeditiously as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory dates set baseline deadlines; agencies must act promptly and expeditiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If structural changes to facilities will be undertaken to achieve program accessibility, the agency shall develop, by February 23, 1987, a transition plan setting forth the steps necessary to complete such changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must provide opportunity for interested persons (including handicapped persons and organizations) to participate by submitting oral and written comments, must be available for public inspection, and at minimum must (1) identify physical obstacles, (2) describe methods to make facilities accessible, (3) specify schedule and annual steps if period >1 year, and (4) indicate the official responsible for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: New construction and alterations standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Each building or part of a building constructed or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of the agency shall be designed, constructed, or altered so as to be readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions, requirements, and standards of the Architectural Barriers Act (42 U.S.C. 4151–4157) and implementing regulations (41 CFR 101–19.600 to 101–19.607) apply to buildings covered by this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective communication obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall take appropriate steps to ensure effective communication with applicants, participants, personnel of other Federal entities, and members of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes furnishing appropriate auxiliary aids where necessary to afford equal opportunity; in determining type of aid, give primary consideration to the requests of the handicapped person; agency need not provide individually prescribed devices, personal readers, or other personal devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone and TDD requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the agency communicates with applicants and beneficiaries by telephone, telecommunication devices for deaf persons (TDDs) or equally effective telecommunication systems shall be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telecommunications must be accessible; alternatives must be equally effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information availability and signage
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall ensure persons with impaired vision or hearing can obtain information about the existence and location of accessible services, activities, and facilities. The agency shall provide signage at primary entrances to inaccessible facilities directing users to where they can obtain information about accessible facilities, and the international symbol for accessibility shall be used at each primary entrance of an accessible facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signage and information provision are required to enable access; use established international symbol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental alteration / undue burden exception and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections on program accessibility and communications do not require actions that the agency can demonstrate would result in a fundamental alteration of the nature of a program or activity or in undue financial and administrative burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency personnel who believe compliance would fundamentally alter or impose undue burdens bear the burden of proving this. The decision must be made by the agency head or designee after considering all agency resources and must be accompanied by a written statement of reasons. If action would cause such alteration/burdens, the agency must take any other action that would not cause such alteration/burdens but still ensure handicapped persons receive benefits and services to the maximum extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint processing jurisdiction and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall accept and investigate all complete complaints for which it has jurisdiction; complete complaints must be filed within 180 days of the alleged act of discrimination (agency may extend for good cause). If agency lacks jurisdiction, it shall notify complainant and make reasonable efforts to refer the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must notify the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board for complaints alleging certain accessibility violations. Within 180 days of receipt of a complete complaint for which it has jurisdiction, the agency shall notify the complainant of results in a letter containing findings of fact and conclusions of law, description of a remedy for each violation found, and notice of right to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals procedure and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals of findings or remedies must be filed by the complainant within 90 days of receipt of the agency letter (agency may extend). Timely appeals shall be accepted and processed by the head of the agency, who shall notify the complainant of the results of the appeal within 60 days. If additional information is needed, the head has 60 days from receipt of that information to make a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits in the investigation and appeal steps may be extended with permission of the Assistant Attorney General.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and limits on investigation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may delegate its authority for conducting complaint investigations to other Federal agencies, except that the authority for making the final determination may not be delegated to another agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigatory functions may be delegated but final decision-making must remain with the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall notify the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board upon receipt of any complaint alleging that a building or facility subject to the Architectural Barriers Act or section 502 of the Rehabilitation Act is not readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures coordination with statutory compliance overseers when buildings/facilities are alleged noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carve-out for statutorily-limited programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The exclusion of nonhandicapped persons from the benefits of a program limited by Federal statute or Executive order to handicapped persons, or the exclusion of a specific class of handicapped persons from a program limited by Federal statute or Executive order to a different class of handicapped persons, is not prohibited by this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation does not override explicit statutory or Executive Order limits that restrict program beneficiaries by disability status or subclass.
